title: Localization: the perception service, the continuous feed, tracking and memory
tagline: One always-on process sees every frame; commands read its states and keep beliefs.
summary: The perception service is a long-running process that looks at the game 15 times a second and turns each frame into a WorldState: her place and HUD, every monster on screen matched to a numbered track, the drops, and events such as deaths (with who killed them), EXP gains and touches. Commands attach over a named pipe and copy frames from shared memory; the simulator runs the same step in-process (SyncFeed). In each command, passive beliefs keep what one frame can't: Memory (monsters seen anywhere), Aggro (who she hurt and is chasing her) and the SpawnClock (when the server refills the map).
details_md:
This slice is the *continuous* side of localization: the game is looked at all the time, by one process, and every
command reads the latest of what it saw. It answers "what is on screen right now, and what just happened?" and keeps a
few beliefs that one frame can't hold.

### Two kinds of process

```
 perception service: python -m gamelab perceive          each command: hunt, nav, tour, pet, watch, hunt look ...
 (one per PC, never sends a key)                         (any number, attach and detach as they start and end)
 +--------------------------------------------+          +------------------------------------------------+
 | ScreenFrames -> feed.run, 15 frames/s      |  state   | ServiceClient (a Feed) on its own thread       |
 |   WorldStep.step (worldstate.py)           | -------> |   keeps the 8 newest states, queues events     |
 |     her look  ||  whole-screen search      |  pipe    | Senses.look -> Feed.look -> to_scene -> Scene  |
 |     ExpMeter (gains.py) -> MonsterTracker  | <------- |   listeners: Memory, SpawnClock, Aggro, ...    |
 |     drops, deaths, touches                 | ask,     |                                                |
 | Ring in shared memory: 16 look frames,     | throw,   | frame_of: copy a look frame out by slot + seq  |
 |   2 full-size frames      ----------------------------> full_frame: copy a full-size one              |
 +--------------------------------------------+          +------------------------------------------------+
```

The **perception service** (`service.py`) is a long-running process started by `python -m gamelab perceive` (or by a
client's `ensure`, or the babysitter). One runs per PC (a named mutex). It owns the PC's only screen capture
(`ScreenFrames`), runs the frame loop (`feed.run`) and, once a frame, the world step (`worldstate.WorldStep.step`).
It never presses a key and never brings the game to the front.

Each **command** talks to it through a `ServiceClient`, which is a `feed.Feed`: the interface `Senses` reads every
look and glance from. In the simulator it is `SyncFeed` (the same step, in-process, on the fake clock); on saved frames
and in unit tests, `InlineFeed`.

### What crosses the boundary

| direction | message | what it carries |
|---|---|---|
| command to service | `hello` | its name, pid, whether it sends keys (`acts`), tells her throws (`throws`), hunts (`fast`), its map |
| command to service | `ask` | an `Asks`: a frame shown at `after` or later, and the drops wanted searched on it |
| command to service | `throw` | her throw's key time and side, optionally her attack's id and the monster it was aimed at |
| command to service | `full`, `status`, `bye` | a full-size frame request; the service's status; leaving |
| service to command | `welcome`, `epoch` | the run's number, map, the next map, the rings' shared-memory names and shapes |
| service to command | `state` | one `WorldState` per frame, its picture removed (its ring `slot` set instead), pickled once |
| service to command | `full`, `gap`, `refused`, `status` | a full frame's slot; how many states a slow reader lost; why it was refused |

Pictures never go down the pipe: the look frames sit in a shared-memory `Ring` (16 slots, about 1.07 s at 15 frames a
second) and a command copies one out by slot and frame number.

### One pass a frame

Since 2026-10-30 everything is read once a frame at 15 frames a second (`localization.rate.HZ`; the user: "I meant
everything at 15 fps"). A pass does her look and the whole screen's search at once on two threads, places her,
reads her EXP, HP and touches, looks for newborns fading in at spawn points, matches every detection to a numbered
track (`tracking.MonsterTracker`), reads HP bars where due, looks for deaths, and searches drops (what was asked, plus
one strip by rotation). A command's ask never gets a frame of its own; it rides on the next frame due.

### Who killed what

The game never says which monster died. Her EXP number goes up 0.1-0.6 s after her attack key while the victim is
still drawn alive. `gains.ExpMeter` turns the number's change into kills by kind (each kind's EXP per kill is the game
data's), and the tracker binds each kill to the track her attack took, follows it until its death is seen or it is
gone, and lets go if it turns up alive. A monster hidden past 3.5 s with no gain of hers on it is someone else's
kill, or let go without a death (lost beside one of its kind, or no other player by it).

### Beliefs kept across looks (in the command)

Three passive listeners run after each look in the command process, fed by the look's `Scene` and events:
`memory.Memory` (every monster seen anywhere, with a probability it's still there), `aggro.Aggro` (who she hurt and
is chasing her for 3-4 minutes) and `spawnclock.SpawnClock` (the server's spawn pass every 7.1146 s, learned from
newborns). They change nothing by themselves; the hunt, the navigator, targeting and the spawn guard ask them.

### Words used here

- **frame**: one capture of the game window. **look**: what a command asks the feed for before it decides
  (`Senses.look`, localization/senses.py); its answer is a **Scene**, that frame placed on the map. A **glance** waits
  for the next state and asks for nothing.
- **track**: one monster followed frame to frame under a number, per **run** (`epoch`): a new map or a restarted
  service starts a run with new rings and new numbers.
- **Shape**: her character's attack reach and timing windows (gamelab/character.py), the thief's by default.

modules.title: Perception service
modules.tagline: The always-on process that perceives every frame and serves states to commands.
modules.summary: Both sides of the perception service. `Service` is the process started by `python -m gamelab perceive` (one per PC, a named mutex) that runs the frame loop on the screen and pushes each frame's WorldState to every attached command over a named pipe, its frames in shared memory. `ServiceClient` is a command's side: a `Feed` that Senses reads, which connects, reconnects and starts the service when none runs. `Publisher` and `Perf` write its telemetry and console line.
modules.details_md:
**Why one process.** On 2026-10-25 the user asked that "perception should just always run and the other modules just
work based on latest perception result", via "one shared perception process at all times". Before, each command had its
own feed child and its own screen duplication (a third DXGI duplication failed with 0x887A0022). Now `ScreenFrames` is
made only here (tests/test_architecture.py checks), and the service never sends a key.

**Threads in the service process.** The main thread runs the frame loop (`Service.serve` calling `feed.run`).
`perceive-accept` takes new pipe connections. Each client gets a `perceive-reader-<id>` thread (its requests) and a
`perceive-writer-<id>` thread (`Writer`, its states). `perceive-watchdog` ends the process with exit code 3 when the
loop hasn't gone round for `STUCK_S` (10 s; 60 s while a run is built), so a client's `ensure` or the babysitter starts
another. The world step adds its own `wide` search thread.

**Runs (`epoch`).** `_build` makes a `feed.Runner` for the map (`screen_world`: ScreenFrames on the process's one
DXGI duplication, Eyes with the map's monster templates and minimap picture, Senses with her Shape, a WorldStep) and two
new shared-memory rings, then tells every client (`epoch`). A run starts when the game is first seen or the map
changes. The map is *held* by commands that hunt (`Hello.fast`): a second hunting command on another map is refused,
saying why. A viewer or `pet` moves it only while no hunt holds it (`_hello`, and `_follow` when a client leaves).

**Asks.** Clients don't get frames of their own. `_read` puts each `ask`, `throw` and `full` in the frame loop's inbox;
`_poll` merges asks while waiting for the next frame due (mesos only if every asker wanted only mesos). A `full` ask is
answered from the next frame, copied into the full ring (`_answer_fulls`); while the window is a size Alt+Enter mends,
an any-size ask gets the client's picture down the pipe (`glimpse`).

**Sending without blocking.** `_emit` puts the frame in the ring, hands it to the rolling recording and the Lie
Detector tracker by reference, pickles the state once (picture removed) and queues it to every `Writer`. A writer keeps
at most `QUEUE_KEEP` (64, 4.3 s) states, dropping the oldest and sending a `gap` count. Measured before it was built:
a state reaches a client 0.13-0.25 ms after it goes; a frame copies out of the ring in 1-1.6 ms; a client that never
read held the frame loop up 10.5 s with the writes in the loop, never with a writer thread per client.

**No game.** With no window, a minimized one, or a client size other than 1366x768 or 1920x1080 (`window_geometry`),
`_not_visible` sends a state every 0.25 s saying why, and keeps waiting `full` asks.

**The command's side (`ServiceClient`).** A `perceive-client` thread reads the pipe address and authkey from
`lab/perceive.json`, connects, sends `hello`, then loops on `recv` (`_take`). Silent for `SILENT_S` (10 s), it drops
and reconnects every `RECONNECT_S` (0.5 s); while it can't, it calls `ensure`, which starts `python -m gamelab perceive`
detached through WMI (PowerShell `Win32_Process.Create`) at most every `ENSURE_EVERY_S` (10 s), its console in
`lab/perceive.log`. `latest(want)` returns the newest kept state that's `feed.fresh` for the look, sending one `ask`
and waiting up to 0.6 s if none is. States of an older run are dropped; a command that sends keys is handed states only
once the service looks at its map (`on_map`). `frame_of` copies the look frame out of the ring; one already
overwritten comes back black and is counted (`lost`). `bring_forward` (commands that send keys only) brings the game
window to the front at most once a second.

**Telemetry.** `Publisher` writes what `watch` used to: a `scene` every 0.1 s, `tracks` every 0.5 s, an `event` for
deaths, gains, victims, let-gos, HP and level reads and touches, an `exp` record per gain; `Perf` times each pass for a
`perf` record and the console line every 10 s.

**Saved frames.** `perceive --frames DIR` builds its runs with `feed.saved_world` (each PNG `--hold` frames in a row,
round and round) at its own pipe, mutex and `lab/perceive-saved.json`, with no telemetry, recording or Lie Detector
tracking; a command reaches it only with `GAMELAB_PERCEIVE=saved`. `serve_saved` is the same as a child process's
target (sim.soak, offline measurements).

key_items.name: Service
key_items.signature: Service(make, map_id, geometry, *, address=ADDRESS, authkey=None, info=None, log=print, publish=None, hz=HZ, stuck_s=None, glimpse=None, recording=None, lie_tracking=None)
key_items.summary: The service process: its clients, its run (Runner, rings, epoch), its inbox of asks, and the frame loop. `make(map_id, geo)` builds what it looks with: screen_world live, feed.saved_world offline.
key_items.details_md: `clients` maps an id to `_Client` (its pipe, `Writer`, `Hello`). `_inbox` holds (client, message) pairs for the frame loop; `_fulls` the full-frame requests waiting for a frame. `counts` keeps connected, states, dropped, fulls, epochs and refused for `status`.

key_items.name: Service.serve
key_items.signature: def serve(self, until: float | None = None) -> None
key_items.summary: The main loop: opens the pipe (`listen`), starts the watchdog, the recording and the Lie Detector tracker, then builds a run when needed and runs feed.run on it until stopped.
key_items.details_md: When `_build` fails (no game window) it calls `_not_visible` and loops. `feed.run` returns when `_poll` says stop or a rebuild is due (a new map), and the loop builds the next run.

key_items.name: Service._hello
key_items.signature: def _hello(self, c: _Client, hello: Hello) -> None
key_items.summary: A client's `hello`: welcomed with the run's ring names, or refused when it hunts (`fast`) on another map than the one a hunting command holds. Any client naming another map moves the service there (a new run) while no hunting command holds the current one.
key_items.details_md: Viewers and `pet` never get refused: they move the map only while no hunting command holds it. `_follow` re-decides when a client leaves: the newest acting command's map wins.

key_items.name: Service._build
key_items.signature: def _build(self) -> bool
key_items.summary: A new run: the map's Runner on the window's geometry, a new look Ring (RING_SLOTS) and full Ring (FULL_SLOTS), `epoch` + 1 broadcast to every client, the old run's rings unlinked.
key_items.details_md: False while the window can't be read. If the map's minimap picture won't load, the run before goes on. Ends with `gcstats.freeze`: everything loaded so far is left alone by the garbage collector.

key_items.name: Service._poll
key_items.signature: def _poll(self, wait: float) -> tuple[Asks | None, bool]
key_items.summary: feed.run's `poll`: drains the inbox (asks merged by `_take`, throws told to the step, full asks kept), waiting up to `wait` s; says stop when asked to or a new run is due.
key_items.details_md: `_take` merges asks with `Asks.merge`, keeping `mesos_only` only if every asker wanted only mesos; a `throw` goes straight to `WorldStep.throw`; a `full` ask also becomes an Asks for its time.

key_items.name: Service._emit
key_items.signature: def _emit(self, st: WorldState, frame) -> None
key_items.summary: feed.run's `emit`: the frame into the ring (its slot in the state), the frame to the recording and Lie Detector tracking by reference, the state without its picture pickled once and queued to every client, then published.
key_items.details_md: `_send_state` does the pickling and queuing; the Publisher sees the full state (with picture).

key_items.name: Service._answer_fulls
key_items.signature: def _answer_fulls(self, frame, st: WorldState | None) -> None
key_items.summary: Answers waiting `full` asks: with this frame copied into the full ring, or with why there's none; an any-size ask while the window needs Alt+Enter gets the client's picture down the pipe (`glimpse`).

key_items.name: Service._watchdog
key_items.signature: def _watchdog(self) -> None
key_items.summary: Ends the process (os._exit(EXIT_STUCK), code 3) once the frame loop hasn't gone round for STUCK_S (BUILD_STUCK_S while building a run), flushing telemetry first, so another service is started.
key_items.details_md: Before it, a hung loop with its pipe up was noticed by nobody: every look found nothing to act on and a hunt stood still to its end.

key_items.name: Writer
key_items.signature: Writer(conn, keep: int = QUEUE_KEEP, name: str = 'perceive-writer')
key_items.summary: A client's pipe written by a thread of its own from a queue of at most QUEUE_KEEP states; older ones are dropped and a `gap` count is sent, so a client that doesn't read never holds anything up.
key_items.details_md: Messages for this client alone (welcome, epoch, full answers: `put(..., keep=True)`) are never dropped and go first. A pipe's buffer is 8 KB and a write waits until it's read.

key_items.name: ServiceClient
key_items.signature: ServiceClient(name, *, acts=False, throws=False, fast=None, map_id=None, title='', address=None, info=None, ensure=ensure, log=print, start=True)
key_items.summary: The service from a command's side: a feed.Feed that Senses reads. A `perceive-client` thread connects, sends `hello`, takes states, events, welcomes and answers; reconnects and starts the service when needed.
key_items.details_md: Keeps the 8 newest states (`KEEP`) and up to EVENTS_KEPT events for the next drain; counts `gaps`, `stale` (older run), `lost` (ring frame overwritten), `served`, `refused`.

key_items.name: ServiceClient.latest
key_items.signature: def latest(self, want: Asks, timeout: float = feed.FEED_WAIT_S, ask: bool = True) -> WorldState | None
key_items.summary: The newest kept state fresh for the look (feed.fresh); if none, sends one `ask` (feed.to_ask) and waits up to FEED_WAIT_S. Returns None at once when the newest state, shown at or after the look's time, isn't usable (the game not wholly on screen, or a failed check).

key_items.name: ServiceClient.on_map
key_items.signature: def on_map(self) -> bool
key_items.summary: Whether the states handed out are of this command's map: a command that acts on a map gets only states of the service's run on it (and its events only then).

key_items.name: ServiceClient.frame_of
key_items.signature: def frame_of(self, st: WorldState) -> np.ndarray
key_items.summary: The state's look frame copied out of the shared ring by slot and frame number; black (counted in `lost`) if the ring has overwritten it since.

key_items.name: ensure
key_items.signature: def ensure(map_id: int | None = None, log: Callable[[str], None] = print) -> bool
key_items.summary: Starts `python -m gamelab perceive` (this checkout, console to lab/perceive.log) unless one runs, at most every ENSURE_EVERY_S, detached through WMI so it outlives the command that started it.
key_items.details_md: Nothing is started for the saved-frames service (GAMELAB_PERCEIVE=saved). The command line carries the character named by the environment and OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1.

key_items.name: Publisher
key_items.signature: Publisher(band: tuple[float, float], log=print)
key_items.summary: The service's telemetry, as `watch` published it: `session` at a run's start, `scene` every SCENE_S, `tracks` every TRACKS_S, an `event` per death/gain/victim/let-go/HP and level read/touch, an `exp` per gain, and the console line with `Perf`'s 'perf' record every STATUS_S.
key_items.details_md: `Perf` gathers each pass's time (median, p90, p99, max), her look's and the whole screen's in it, detections and tracks a frame, newborns and exact finds a minute, the state's age as it goes out, and the process's cores.

inputs: Game frames from perception.frames.ScreenFrames (the PC's one DXGI duplication), or saved PNGs offline
Each client's messages over the named pipe: hello, ask, throw, full, status, bye
The map to look at: `perceive --map`, then the map of the commands that hunt
The game window's geometry (window.find_game and its client size)
outputs: A WorldState per frame (picture removed) pickled down the pipe to every attached command
Look frames in a shared-memory Ring (16 slots) and full-size frames in another (2 slots)
Telemetry records (session, scene, tracks, event, exp, perf) into the run's lab/telemetry/<time>-perceive.jsonl

Its frames, by reference, to control.recording (the rolling recording) and to the Lie Detector tracking that `perceive` hands it (control.lie_tracking together with control.violetta_live's Violetta answers)
A console line every 10 s: frames a second, who's attached, monsters followed, deaths, EXP a minute, the pass's time

modules.concurrency: A process of its own (`python -m gamelab perceive`), one per PC (named mutex `Local\gamelab-perceive`), normal priority, OpenCV on one thread, Windows timers at 1 ms (`settle`). Threads: the frame loop (main), `perceive-accept`, a reader and a writer per client, `perceive-watchdog`, and the world step's `wide` search thread. The rolling recording and the Lie Detector tracking handed in by `perceive` run their own workers (the mini-game's tracker in a process of its own); the service only hands them frames, never waiting. Each command runs a `perceive-client` thread for its ServiceClient. `ensure` starts the service detached through WMI, not as the command's child.

decisions.what: One shared perception process looks at the game for every command; the per-command feed child, `--feed`/`--no-feed` and the sweep were removed.
decisions.why: The user: "perception should just always run and the other modules just work based on latest perception result"; how: "run one shared perception process at all times". Each command's own duplication had failed at the third (0x887A0022).

decisions.what: One pace whoever is attached (before: 30 a second while a hunt was attached, 10 otherwise).
decisions.why: The user: "Run the perception at the same rate between hunt and idle. The idea is perception is running as a constant thing and hunt is only a consumer of it". 20 a second cost 7.7% EXP a minute in the harness; 5 between hunts was set back ("Don't reduce perception fps please").

decisions.what: The rolling recording is kept by the service from its own frames.
decisions.why: `gamelab recorder` had kept it with a capture of its own until then.

decisions.what: RING_SLOTS from 8 to 16.
decisions.why: At 30 a second a look's frame was overwritten 86-88 ms after the look had its state at the soonest.

decisions.what: 15 frames a second, everything once a frame.
decisions.why: The user: "I meant everything at 15 fps" (README, Perception at 15 frames a second).

decisions.what: The Lie Detector's mini-game target tracking takes the service's frames.
decisions.why: It replaced the player's YOLO shadow.

decisions.what: A watchdog ends a service whose frame loop hangs (STUCK_S); clients reconnect after SILENT_S.
decisions.why: Found in review: a hung loop with its pipe up was noticed by nobody, and a hunt stood still to its end.

decisions.what: Only commands that hunt hold the service's map.
decisions.why: The pet's babysitter held it as a command that acts, and a hunt on any other map was refused at its start.

decisions.what: `perceive --frames` has its own pipe, mutex and info file.
decisions.why: With the live ones, a run of it kept the live service from starting, and a command acted on saved frames.

gotchas: A client's states have no picture: copy the look frame from the ring with `frame_of` within about 1 s, or it comes back black (counted in `lost`).
Track ids restart with each run: a new map or a restarted service means new ids (Memory matches by place).
A hang that holds Python's lock stops the watchdog thread too: clients drop after SILENT_S and stand still, and nothing ends that process (README, not done).
The service perceives one character (its welcome's `character`); a command that hunts as another refuses to start (`_perceives_her` in gamelab/__main__.py).
A viewer on another map than the one a hunt holds sees that map's places (it says so).
The window at another size is a wait, never a new run: the user, or a command that acts with Alt+Enter twice, sets it right.

modules.title: The feed
modules.tagline: The frame loop and the Feed interface every look reads; SyncFeed for the simulator.
modules.summary: Defines what the stack asks of perception (`Feed`: latest, glance, look, drain_events, throw) and the frame loop `run` that steps the world once a frame at 15 a second, asks riding on the next frame due. Also the shared-memory `Ring` of frames, and two in-process feeds: `SyncFeed`, stepped by the simulator's fake clock, and `InlineFeed`, stepped on demand for saved frames and tests.
modules.details_md:
**Why a separate process.** Python's global lock: a perception thread in the same process as the planner got 16 of its
60 looks in 2 s (the research's gil.py). So live, the frame loop runs in the perception service and the stack reads
finished states. In the simulator that cost doesn't exist (time is fake), so `SyncFeed` runs the same step in-process.

**The frame loop (`run`).** Each period (1/HZ s, 15 a second) it calls `poll(wait)` to collect asks until the next
frame is due, merging them into `pending`. At the due time it takes `runner.frames.next(due)`.
- Not visible: a state carrying the problem goes to `emit`, `Runner.recover` lets the eyes re-find the minimap picture
  and her name tag (at most every `RECOVER_EVERY_S`, 0.2 s), and the loop waits `NOT_VISIBLE_S` (0.25 s).
- `shown(frame)` sees the frame before the pass (the service answers `full` asks with it).
- An unchanged screen nobody asked about (`frame.new` False) is skipped.
- Otherwise `WorldStep.step` runs, given the pending asks if the frame is late enough for them, and `emit` gets the
  state; a failed check calls `recover`.
- The next due time stays on the grid (`due + period`), or now if the loop is behind.

Since 2026-10-30 a look never gets a frame of its own: what it asks rides on the next frame due. As first built a
frame asked for was taken at once and the grid re-phased, 15.7-15.9 frames a second in the simulator's standard grind.

**Freshness (`fresh`).** A state is good for a look when it is usable (visible, no `bad` problem), shown at
`want.after` or later (1e-9 s slack), and, if the look wants drops, searched for them on that very frame (a pile just
picked up must not be seen again). Her place, the HUD and every monster are in every state, so `to_ask` only ever asks
for a time and drops. A state where she isn't placed still counts: it is what a look would have been.

**What the stack asks (`Feed`).**
- `latest(want)`: the newest fresh state, asking once and waiting up to `FEED_WAIT_S` (0.6 s); None makes Senses try
  again (it gives up with LookLost after 3 s of nothing).
- `glance(after)`: waits up to `GLANCE_WAIT_S` (0.25 s) for any newer state, asking nothing.
- `look(...)`: `latest` plus `worldstate.to_scene` into the stack's `Scene`. A band look also gets the rest of the
  screen's monsters in `Scene.swept` (which Memory takes) and the rows searched in `Scene.rows`.
- `drain_events(upto)`: every event once, only up to the frame the look shows.
- `newest(after)`: the newest usable state with no wait and no ask (the hunter's last look before a key).
- `throw(...)`: her throw, for the tracker.

**The Ring.** One `SharedMemory` block: first a 16-byte head per slot (frame number and time, two float64s), then
the slots' RGB frames. `put`
writes the number as -1 first, then the picture, then time and number; `get` copies and re-checks the number, so a
copy torn by a write returns None. Frame shape is `frame_shape(geo)`: (540, 960, 3) at 1920x1080 (half size), (768,
1366, 3) at the game's own 1366x768.

**SyncFeed (the simulator).** The simulator's clock calls `tick(t)` at every game frame (`GAME_HZ` 60). A frame is
stepped `hz` times a second; its state becomes readable `Costs.of(state)` later and the next frame waits for that. The
costs are the live pass's at 1366x768: capture 2 ms, her look 8.5, the whole screen 8.4 beside it plus 1.8 for running
both, a bar 1.1, a death look 0.8, a strip of drops 3.8. Waiting goes through the simulator's own `time.sleep`, so
nothing is charged to the stack's time.

**InlineFeed.** Each look steps one frame on the eyes' own capture, with no drop rotation (`drops_strips=0`). Used by
`bench-look`, saved frames and the unit tests; `Senses` makes one when it was given no feed.

modules.title: World step and WorldState
modules.tagline: One pass a frame: her look, every monster tracked, drops, EXP, HP and touches.
modules.summary: `WorldStep.step` turns one game frame into a `WorldState`: plain, picklable data about her place and HUD, every monster on screen with its track id, the drops, and the events of that frame. It runs inside the perception service (or SyncFeed/InlineFeed) and drives the detectors, the EXP meter (gains.py) and the tracker (tracking.py). `to_scene` turns a state back into the `Scene` a look of the stack would have made.
modules.details_md:
**The pass (`step`), in order.**
1. `_search_ahead` starts the whole-screen monster search (`MobDetector.detect_wide` over the play area above the
   bottom bar, and the exact finder after it) on the step's own thread; meanwhile the caller's thread does her look
   (`Eyes.look_at`: name tag, minimap dot, HP, MP, EXP pixels, ropes, other players). Both are mostly C that lets go of
   Python's lock: 10.3 ms together against 15.95 one after the other (`HALVES`).
2. `senses.place` puts her on the map; `_vitals` reads EXP, HP and touches into events.
3. `_newborns`: the spawn watch looks at every spawn point in view for a monster fading in (Tree Dungeon only,
   `spawns.MEASURED`); it found 229 of 233 newborns at their first visible frame, a median 7 frames (467 ms) before
   the whole screen did. `_handed` adds them as detections (with their alpha) until the search finds them.
4. `_wide` waits for the search; `_exact_added` adds the exact finder's finds where no detection lies.
5. Each detection is placed on the map and given to `MonsterTracker.update` with the `View` (what the frame shows of
   the map), her place, other players, a bar reader (`_reader`) and a death check (`_dying`).
6. `_drops`: the strips a look asked for, searched whole on this frame; then one strip by rotation.
7. All of it goes into a `WorldState`, with `work` timings (`s`, `look s`, `wide s`, ...).

**HP bars (`_bar_due`).** A bar read costs 1.1 ms. A track's bar is read when it showed one within `BAR_SHOWN_S`
(0.25 s), it was hidden or unseen for `BAR_UNSEEN_S` (0.15 s) or more, a throw of hers went its way in the star window,
or `BAR_EVERY_S` (0.2 s, every third frame) has passed; a new track's always. Otherwise the state carries the track's
last bar. Read in every frame, bars were 74% of what the simulator's feed cost. With the exact finder, a bar that could
be an overlapping neighbour's isn't read (`hud.bar_shared`).

**Deaths (`_dying`, `_died_seen`).** Tracks found weakly in the frame or lost lately are matched against the game
data's die1 frames where their feet are (perception.deaths, at most every `deaths.EVERY_S`). The exact finder's die1
finds name a death too; one animation counts once (`DIE_ONE_NEAR` 12 units, `DIE_ONE_S` 0.9 s). Seen deaths reach the
tracker before her gains are judged.

**EXP, HP, touches (`_vitals`).** When the EXP number's pixels change (`hud.exp_changed`), it is read
(perception.exp_number) and `gains.ExpMeter` says what the change was; `_told` tells the tracker one kill per kind at its
time, and a share for an odd gain. An `exp_gain` event carries the reading and, since 2026-11-02, the reading `before`
it. HP falling more than `HP_DROP` (0.004) is an `hp_drop`; a new drop with no popup told within `TOUCH_SAME_S` (1 s)
is a touch by HP. Touches come from the touch watch's popups (MISS or damage); a MISS followed by an HP drop within
`touches.HP_WAIT_S` is re-told as damage (`touch_fix`). A touch told off a popup that isn't damage (a MISS, or
unread) while another player's dot is within 60 x 60 units of her is marked `crowded`: the popup may be theirs. Her HP number and level digits are read at each change (`hp_read`, `lv_read`).

**Drops (`_drops`).** Asked-for strips (her platform's, or every platform's in view) are searched on the frame asked.
The rotation searches `DROPS_STRIPS` (1) strip every `DROPS_EVERY_S` (0.2 s), the one searched longest ago first, her
platform's counted twice as old (`DROPS_HER`), only on a frame placed firmly in height (`_firm`). `WorldState.drops`
lists every strip in view with when it was last searched and what it had.

**Plain data.** `WorldState` holds no map objects. The service drops its picture before pickling; the EXP pixels are
packed with `np.packbits`. `to_scene` rebuilds the `Scene` a look would have made: her place, the monsters in her band
(or all with `wide`), the drops asked for.

decisions.what: One pass a frame at 15 a second, every monster from that frame's whole screen.
decisions.why: Replaces 30 a second with re-finds and a search thread merged frames later (`late`). On the crowd's 900-frame replay the whole screen alone at 15 took 0.503 cores, against 0.683 for the old design at 15 and at least 0.752 at 30, with the tracker's outcomes about the same; in the service bench each state left 13 ms after its frame with that frame's whole screen, where master's newest whole screen was 70 ms old.

decisions.what: Drops by rotation: one strip every 0.2 s.
decisions.why: Two strips every frame, as designed, took the frame loop 0.77-0.80 cores against 0.43 with none.

decisions.what: The rotation only on a frame placed firmly in height (`_firm`).
decisions.why: Review: strips placed by her offset in the air saw 15 of 49 and 15 of 53 piles as gone with their coins still there.

decisions.what: The spawn watch looks at every spawn point in view on every frame.
decisions.why: The user: "Should probably always check instead of only checking when it's due"; of a looser search anywhere: "I'd like to avoid that" (false positives). It found 229 of 233 newborns at their first visible frame.

decisions.what: Her HP number and level digits read at each change ('hp_read', 'lv_read'); a MISS that took HP re-told as damage (FIX_MISS, after that day's review).
decisions.why: One MISS of 269 touches on the hunting frames of 2026-10-24..28 had a drop so; before, her knock was never waited out.

decisions.what: 'exp_gain' events carry `before`, the reading before the change.
decisions.why: A hunt attaching after the service read it starts from it (behavior.hunter).

decisions.what: Bars read by schedule, not every frame (BAR_EVERY_S).
decisions.why: Read in every frame, the bars were 74% of what the simulator's feed cost.

The spawn watch runs only on maps in perception.spawns.MEASURED (Tree Dungeon) with its C built.
A frame that fails its checks (`bad`) has its EXP and HP ignored and her HP number forgotten: the next good frame is compared instead.
A state's `loot` is only what was asked on that frame; `drops` is every strip in view as last searched.
`band`, `wide`, `band_at`, `wide_at` and `late` are kept only for older clients: every state has her band and the whole screen.

A track's bar carried over from an older read can sit on an unhurt monster: at the simulator's -80 rope arrivals, 97 of the 118 bars on unhurt monsters were kept from older reads (README, Her aggro belief). The aggro belief reads a bar only fresh; the perception's own bar is unchanged.

modules.title: EXP gains
modules.tagline: Turns her EXP number's changes into kills by kind, and EXP a minute.
modules.summary: `ExpMeter` follows her EXP number as it's read (perception.exp_number) and says what each change was: how many kills, of which kinds (each kind's EXP per kill is the game data's), or not a kill at all. Two run: the world step's, whose kills go to the tracker for kill credit, and the hunter's, for its kill counts and EXP a minute.
modules.details_md:
**Sizes name kinds.** Each kind's EXP per kill is the game data's (`MapModel.mob_exp`; on Thicket Around the Beach II
a snail 2, a slime 12, a pig 13, an Orange Mushroom 15) times `EXP_RATE` (1.0). A change of 13 there is one pig.
`split` looks for the fewest kills (up to `SPLIT_KILLS`, 4) whose EXP adds up to the change; when only one set of kinds
of that count does, the kinds are named, else each is None (39 is three pigs, or two slimes and an Orange Mushroom:
three kills of kinds not known). A change no kills add up to is `odd` (a party share, a quest): not a kill. The world
step tells the tracker an odd positive gain as a *share*.

**Suspicious changes wait.** A change worth more than `JUMP_KILLS` (4) of the map's best kill (at least `JUMP_LEAST`,
30 EXP), a fall (a death costs EXP) or a level that doesn't follow is `held` until a second reading agrees; one that
doesn't is dropped as a misreading. Across a level-up (`_since`) a gain is what was left of the old level (from the EXP
table, `maplehelper/ocr/exp_table.py`) plus what's into the new one.

**Changes it couldn't read.** The cursor or a window over the number changes its pixels with no readable value. Such
changes are grouped into bursts (`ALONE_S`, 0.5 s apart); the first burst is the cover coming. The next good reading
says how much EXP came, and `_end_run` places that many kills at the latest bursts' times. A lone burst still
unexplained after `UNREAD_WAIT_S` (1.5 s) becomes one kill of a kind not known (`due`). So a cursor passing over the
number is no kill (before, it counted two).

**Reading pace.** While the number has no value, `wants_reading` asks for a reading `RETRY_S` (0.5 s) after the last
try, doubling to `RETRY_MAX_S` (8 s): retrying every 0.5 s had cost 17-20 ms a second.

**The rate check (`_check`).** Of the last `RATE_GAINS` (8) gains from one change each, fewer than `RATE_OFF` (4)
being one kill turns the sizes off (an EXP event or coupon): each change is then one kill of a kind not known, and a
note says which rate of 0.5-3 the gains fit. `RATE_ON` (6) turns them back on. Until 6 of the first 8 have been one kill
each, a gain is named when it's one kill but never split (at rate 2 every kill would read as two). Without the check, at rate 1.5 six kills had counted 12-14.

**EXP a minute.** `per_minute` is the EXP gained since the first reading over the time since (None in the first 10 s).

modules.title: Monster tracker
modules.tagline: Gives every monster an id frame to frame, and decides who killed it.
modules.summary: `MonsterTracker` matches each frame's whole-screen detections to numbered tracks, predicts where unseen ones walk, and turns what happens into events (entered, spawned, back, left, bar_hit, died, victim, let_go). Its hardest job is kill credit: the game never says which monster died, so each EXP gain is bound to the monster her attack took and followed until its death is confirmed or it is let go.
modules.details_md:
**Matching (`_match`).** Each frame's detections (the whole screen's) are paired with tracks of the same kind on the
same platform within a gate of `MATCH_BASE` + `MATCH_SPEED` x speed x time since + `MATCH_KNOCKBACK` (10 + 1.3 x speed x
dt + 25 units: 43.7 a frame on at 15 a second) of where the track should be (`predicted`). Pairs are taken greedily,
nearest first. A walking track met by a detection facing the other way, away from its platform's ends, costs
`FACING_COST` (8 units) more: two of a kind passing keep their ids. Special gates: a dying track with no gain on it
takes a detection only within `FADE_MOVE` (10 units); a bound victim lost after her star landed refuses far sightings
(`_stray`); a sighting fading in only matches a track first seen after its fade began.

**Motion from game data.** A track's place is its last detection's feet. Its velocity is not measured: it is its
kind's walk speed from the game data in the way its pose faces (a move frame walks, a stand or hit1 frame stands:
`monsters.walk_vx`). `predicted` walks it on for at most `EXTRAPOLATE_S` (0.5 s), folding back at its platform's walk
edges.

**New tracks (`_new`).** `spawned` if found fading in; else `entered` if within `EDGE_PX` (24 half-size px) of the
screen's edge (the camera moved, or it walked in); else `spawned` if within `SPAWN_NEAR` (60 units) of a spawn point of
its kind on its platform; else `appeared`.

**Tracks not seen (`_unseen`).** Off screen: `offscreen` (event `left`), remembered `OFFSCREEN_S` (10 s) to recognise
it coming `back`. On screen and unseen `MISSING_S` (0.3 s): `hidden` (a hit monster flinches under its damage numbers
for 1-3 s). Seen in fewer than 3 frames (`MIN_SEEN_S` 0.2 s) and gone: a flicker, dropped with no death (never a newborn seen
fading in). Hidden longer than `HIDE_S` (3.5 s from its last sighting, or from `HIT_AFTER_S`, 1.2 s, after her last
throw its way if that's later): dead, cause "other" (`died`), naming the other player by
it, unless it vanished beside one of its kind ("lost in a crowd") or no other player's minimap dot was by it
(`OTHERS_BY_PLAYER`: "nobody by it"); both are let go without a death.

**Her kills (`_resolve`, `_bind`, `_picks`).** Worldstate tells `gain(t, kind)` for each kill her EXP gain names. A
gain within `BIND_S` (0.3 s) and 0.1-0.6 s after a throw's key (`GAIN_AFTER_KEY`) is bound to the first of `_picks`:
the tracks of that kind ahead of where she was `PICK_S` (65 ms) after the key, from `VICTIM_BEHIND` (20) behind to her
reach ahead (`THROW_REACH`, 474), `VICTIM_UP` (110) above her feet to `VICTIM_DOWN` (75) below, those seen in the last
`FRESH_S` (0.2 s) first, nearest first. For the magician (her Shape's `kill`) `_band_picks` ranks by Magic Claw's own
search bands, oldest track first, as the client picks. `_victim` makes it `dying` with the gain on it and a `victim`
event; it may walk on until her star lands (`STAR_LANDS_S` 0.75 s after the key plus distance / `STAR_FLIGHT` 1490).

**Confirming (`_judge`, `_deaths_seen`).** A bound track is `dead` (cause "hers") when its death is seen, or once
unseen `MISSING_S` from `CONFIRM_S` (1.5 s) after the gain. Seen alive `REBIND_S` (1.2 s) after the gain, it was the
wrong one: `let_go`, and the gain moves to the next pick now out of sight. A death seen on another of the gain's picks
takes the gain from the bound one; a death seen with a gain waiting takes that gain (only `DEATH_AFTER_GAIN_S`, 0.3 s,
or more after it); otherwise it is someone else's kill. A gain with no throw known (`watch`) waits `FADE_S +
MISSING_S` for the likeliest candidate (`_likely`) to vanish. A throw told again the other way re-binds (`_retold`).

On 85 kills labelled by eye on the recordings of 2026-10-25/26 the binding found the truth's track 76 times (89%); the
hunt's older ledger had 52 right.

**Bounded.** Dead tracks go `DEAD_KEEP_S` (2 s) after death, offscreen ones after 10 s; throws, picks and gains after
their windows.

modules.title: Memory of monsters
modules.tagline: Every monster seen anywhere, kept across looks with how sure it's still there.
modules.summary: `Memory` is a passive Senses listener in the command process that remembers every monster any look has seen, by kind, platform and x. Each entry's chance of still being there falls with age and with looks that covered its place without seeing it; her kills and the tracker's dead tracks end entries. The hunt, grinding, the navigator, localization.unseen and patrol.Belief ask it which monsters are likely where she can't see.
modules.details_md:
**Why.** In the live hunts of 2026-10-24 on Tree Dungeon, 90% of her looks searched only the band around her, and
monsters on other platforms were seen only on whole-screen looks a median 4.9 s apart (up to 22.8 s). The user,
watching: "Right now during the hunt she has tunnelled vision". Since the service, every look carries the whole
screen's monsters (`Scene.swept`), but what isn't on screen still has to be remembered.

**Matching (`update`).** A sighting is a remembered monster when it's the same kind on the same platform within
`MATCH_SLACK` (40 units) plus `MATCH_SPEED` (1.3) x what it can have walked since (at most `MATCH_WALK_S`, 30 s) of
where it was seen; nearest first. A sighting where a monster killed in the last `FADE_S` (1.5 s) can be fading (or
within `FADE_DX`, 30 units, of where its kill was placed) is that corpse, not a new monster.

**Coverage (`Cover.holds`, `_holds`).** A look *covers* a body when the whole of it (as tall as it walks, plus
`BODY_SLACK` 4 units) lay inside one stretch of rows the look searched, `EDGE` (30 units) inside the screen's sides
and not under the minimap: the detector finds only whole bodies, so a cut body is not a miss. An entry counts a miss
when a covering look searched at least `COVER_SHARE` (half) of where it can have walked since, judged at
`COVER_POINTS` (9) places. Looks while she isn't standing don't count (every monster's y is off by her height). Misses
don't count while a throw of hers went its way in the last `HIDE_S` and it was seen since: it may be hiding under her
damage numbers.

**How sure (`Remembered.p`).** p = exp(-age / `STAY_S`) x exp(-d / `MISS_S`), with `STAY_S` 45 s and `MISS_S` 3 s,
d the time from its last sighting to the latest covered miss. Measured on 8,750 whole-screen looks of `watch` on
2026-10-24: monsters missing with their place covered were seen again 0.84 of the time after 0.3 s, 0.51 after 2 s,
0.20 after 5 s, where exp(-d/3) gives 0.90, 0.51, 0.19. An entry is forgotten under `P_FORGET` (0.15, about 5.7 s of
covered misses) or `MEMORY_S` (60 s) after it was seen. `there()` returns those at least `SURE` (0.5) likely.

**Kills (`_take_kills`, `_take_moves`).** The ledger's new kills mark entries killed: by track id when known, else the
nearest of its kind on its platform within `KILL_DX` (150). The feed's dead tracks end their entries too: another
player's kill as `taken`, not `killed`. When the tracker moves a kill to another monster (the magician's kills), the
first entry comes back alive and the new one is killed, as one `moved` event. Unplaced kills (no kind or platform) go on
the likeliest monster she threw at.

**Who reads it.** The hunt (`memory.there`), grinding, the navigator and localization.unseen (`memory.alive`), `patrol.Belief` (its events)
and the mini-map (its 'memory' telemetry records, every `RECORD_EVERY_S` 0.5 s). `update` takes plain data, so
`replay` runs the same memory over a recorded run's 'scene' records.

modules.title: Aggro belief
modules.tagline: Who she hurt and is chasing her, kept for the 3-4 minute chase.
modules.summary: `Aggro` keeps every monster she has hurt as a `Chaser` for as long as its chase lasts (180-240 s after each hit), across looks that don't see it and the tracker's changes of id, and predicts where it is. It also names the monster that likeliest touched her at each touch. Passive, in the command process, fed every look and throw by the hunter. Today behavior.targeting reads which tracks are chasers; the planner's questions (`chasers_at`, `near`, `Guess.track`, `toucher`) have no caller yet.
modules.details_md:
**The rule it models** (the user's, 2026-10-31; the v83 client's `Mob::chase` as HeavenClient has it; the simulator's
`sim.world.AGGRO_S`): an unhurt monster wanders; a hit of hers draws a chase of `CHASE_S` (180-240 s), renewed by each
hit. Chasing, it decides every `THINK_S` (0.945 s) which way to walk: at her, or on its way while she's within
`CHASE_PASS` (100 units) across, so it walks past her and back. It walks at its kind's speed along its own platform,
folding at its walk edges, and after a hit it stands its flinch out first (`monsters.FLINCH_S`).

**Why** (the arrival diagnosis of 2026-11-03): arriving onto Tree Dungeon's platform 10 by the -80 rope, the look held
none of the monsters within 60 of her in about 30% of cases, and nothing kept who she had hurt for the minutes they
chase her (the navigator's trip memory forgets after 2 s; the hunt's wounds after 3 s out of sight).

**Making a chaser (`_bar_hit`).** A `bar_hit` event the tracker says is "hers", or any `bar_hit` up to `LATE_S` (4 s)
after a throw whose path held that track (a hit hidden 1-3 s under damage numbers, past the tracker's window). A hit on
a new track near a lost chaser of its kind (within its reach plus `REJOIN_SLACK`) is that chaser found again under a new
id (`_lost_near`).

**Keeping identity (`_associate`, `_pairs`).** Each look, every chaser goes to one track, nearest its prediction first:
its own track (`OWN_BONUS`, 30 units nearer) while that shows a bar read within `BAR_FRESH_S` (0.5 s) of its sighting;
never another chaser's track; another track only if it was first seen after the chaser was last seen. A track with no
bar read for `BAR_GONE_S` (1.5 s) leaves its chaser doubted (`DOUBT_P` 0.3), dropped as a 'phantom' after `DOUBT_S`
(8 s): a bar misread off a neighbour made it.

**Ending (`_died`, `_follow`, `_end`).** Its death, its track becoming a kill's, `CHASE_S[1]` (240 s) after her last
hit, or `FORGET_S` (120 s) unseen. A death the tracker called another's with nobody by it keeps the chaser, lost, at
`OTHER_DEATH_P` (0.5): the tracker calls any hurt monster hidden past 3.5 s dead.

**Where it is (`_guess`, `_chase_x`).** From its last sighting the chase is played forward decision by decision against
her path for `DET_S` (1 s) unseen, or until it could have reached her, with a reach of `SPREAD_0` (15 units) plus
`SPREAD_RATE` (0.35) of its walk a second unseen either side. Past that it is "about her": her x, `CHASE_PASS` plus a
decision's walk either side, within its walk edges. `p` = the chase still on (1 until 180 s, falling to 0 at 240) x
being about (1 while seen within `SEEN_S` 10 s, then exp(-(unseen - 10) / 60)) x the doubt factors; 0 while dying.

**Touches (`_touched`, `_knocks`).** For each 'touch' event, the candidates are the chasers' guesses and other tracks
walked on (0.5 s at most) at her place at the popup's onset; the one whose reach covers her likeliest is named with its
side. A damage touch's knock (her place moving `KNOCK_DX`, 15 units, or more) puts the side right.

**Measured in the simulator** at the -80 arrivals over 48 seeds: by identity the belief's recall and precision were
82.2% / 75.0% for her (the magician) and 78.2% / 70.7% for him (the thief), against 52.9% / 64.3% and 39.8% / 53.4%
for the look alone (its monsters with a bar). It costs a median 0.035-0.055 ms a look.

**Who asks.** It was built as the per-step planner's prerequisite (README, Her aggro belief), so its questions are
the planner's: `chasers_at`, `near`, `Guess.track` (a `localization.monsters.MonsterTrack` the move planner takes)
and `toucher`. In the code today only behavior.targeting reads it (`aggro.chasers`: which tracks chase her, for a
foe's walk), and the hunter writes its 'aggro' telemetry record every `AGGRO_RECORD_S` (30 s) and at each touch.

modules.title: Spawn clock
modules.tagline: Learns the server's 7.1146 s respawn pass from newborns fading in.
modules.summary: `SpawnClock` learns when the server's next spawn pass will refill free spawn points, from the births perception sees ('spawned' events with their fade-in alpha). The hunt's spawn guard asks it whether the clock is sure, when the next pass is, and how likely a stretch of time meets one.
modules.details_md:
**The server's pass.** The server fills the map's free spawn points at a pass every `PERIOD_S` (7.1146 s), not
monster by monster. Measured on both live hours of 2026-11-02 (3,204 and 1,418 fading sightings over 504 and 379
periods): the same period in every 10 minutes of each; on one hour 95% of newborns' starts lay within 0.1 s of the
fitted passes.

**Births (`see`, `birth`).** For each 'spawned' event (the tracker's, localization.tracking), a monster found fading in
gives its birth time: the event's time less its alpha over `FADE_PER_S` (perception.spawns: 1.224 alpha a second, 0.817
s from nothing to solid). One found already solid by a spawn point counts `SOLID_WEIGHT` (0.3) of one. Births within
`SAME_PASS_S` (0.4 s) are one pass; passes of the last `MEMORY_S` (600 s) are kept.

**The fit (`_fit`).** Each kept pass is a candidate phase; the one with the most age-weighted passes (exp(-age /
`AGE_S`), 300 s) within `INLIER_S` (0.35 s) of its grid wins. Its inliers are then fitted to the grid by weighted least
squares; once they span `PERIOD_SPAN_S` (120 s) and 3 distinct passes, the period is fitted too, held within
`PERIOD_SLACK` (0.05 s) of the default. The residuals' spread (at least `SIGMA_MIN`, 0.03 s) over the square root of
the weight is the phase's standard error. The clock is `sure` once the weight reaches `SURE_N` (1.5: two fading
births agreeing). Fits run lazily when asked (`_dirty`).

**A phase that moves (`_astray_check`, `forget`).** A server restart or a channel change shifts the phase. `ASTRAY_N`
(3) passes in a row with fading births more than `INLIER_S` off a sure clock's grid drop the passes before them, so the
clock follows at once. Before this (the review of 2026-11-03) an hour of the old phase outvoted the new for 24 passes
(171 s). The hunt also calls `forget` after its looks were lost for more than 21 s.

**Answers.** `next_pass(t)`: the first pass after t. `chance(t0, t1, lo, hi)`: how likely the interval [t0, t1]
overlaps [T + lo, T + hi] for some pass T, each pass's time normal about the grid with the fit's standard error;
with no phase yet, the window's share of a period. Replayed on the live hours' newborns it is sure 14 s in and puts
births within 0.055 s of its passes at p95. The simulator's pass (`sim.world.TICK_S`, 7.115 s) is 0.0004 s off, so it
was left as it is.

flows.title: A frame, from the screen to every command
flows.summary: How one game frame becomes a WorldState in the perception service and crosses into each attached command.
flows.trigger: The frame loop's next due time in the perception service (every 1/15 s).

steps.text: The main thread builds a run when needed (`_build`: the map's Runner, new rings, an `epoch` to every client), tunes the step for who's attached (`_tune`) and runs feed.run.

Waits for asks until the frame is due (`Service._poll` drains the inbox and merges every client's asks), then takes `ScreenFrames.next(due)`. A frame not visible gets a state with its problem, a recovery, and a 0.25 s wait.
`full` asks waiting for this frame are answered: the frame is copied into the full-size ring and its slot sent to the asker.
Her look and the whole-screen search at once (two threads), her place, EXP, HP and touches, newborns at spawn points, detections placed on the map.
Detections matched to tracks, the unseen judged, bars read where due, deaths seen, her gains bound to victims; the frame's events returned.

The frame goes into the look Ring (slot = seq mod 16); the rolling recording and Lie Detector tracking get it by reference; the state, picture removed, is pickled once and queued to every client; Publisher writes telemetry.
Each client's writer thread sends its queue down the pipe; a slow reader loses the oldest states (64 kept) and is told a `gap`.
In the command, the client's thread keeps the state (8 newest), drops one of an older run, and queues its events for the next drain (only once the run is on its map).
When Senses looks, the newest fresh state becomes a Scene (`worldstate.to_scene`); the look frame is copied out of the shared ring by slot and frame number (`ServiceClient.frame_of`).

flows.title: A look that needs drops searched, and the beliefs after it
flows.summary: What happens when a command's look needs something not in every state (the drops on her platform), and how the look's events reach the beliefs kept across looks.
flows.trigger: Senses.look in a command (a hunt deciding its next move, with `loot=True`).

steps.text: Works out the earliest acceptable frame time (after the last look's frame, 68 ms after her last key, and at most 0.1 s before now) and calls the feed's look.
The look's arguments become an Asks: `after`, `loot`, `loot_wide`, `mesos_only`.
No kept state was searched for those drops on a late enough frame: `to_ask` sends one `ask` up the pipe, and it waits up to 0.6 s.
The client's reader thread puts the ask in the frame loop's inbox and wakes the loop.
The frame loop merges it with other clients' asks (mesos only if every asker wanted only mesos).
The ask rides on the next frame due shown at its time or later: no frame of its own.
The asked strips are searched whole on that frame, before the rotation's strip, and the state's `loot` is set.
Back in the command, the new state is fresh: shown after `after`, drops searched on it. `to_scene` builds the Scene.
Events up to that frame are drained (each once) into `Scene.events`; then the listeners run: Memory.on_look, the hunter's `_births` (SpawnClock.see) and `_aggro` (Aggro.on_look), among others.
Sightings matched to remembered monsters or new, covered misses counted, kills taken, the unlikely forgotten.
bar_hit events make or renew chasers, each chaser is matched to its track, touches get their likeliest monster.

flows.title: An EXP gain becomes a dead, named monster
flows.summary: The game never says which monster died. This is how a change of her EXP number becomes a `died` event naming a track, cause 'hers'.
flows.trigger: Her EXP number's pixels change in a frame (a kill's EXP shows 0.1-0.6 s after her attack key).

steps.text: Earlier, the hunt told the service her throw (key time, side, attack, aim) through the pipe; the tracker noted which tracks its star could meet from where she was.
`hud.exp_changed` sees the number change; perception.exp_number reads it; an `exp_gain` event goes out.
The change's size is split into kills by kind (13 on Thicket Around the Beach II is a pig), held for a second reading if suspicious, or flagged odd.
Each kill is told to the tracker at its time: `MonsterTracker.gain(t, kind)`.
In the same frame's update, the gain is matched to the throw keyed 0.1-0.6 s before it; `_picks` (or `_band_picks` for the magician) ranks the tracks that attack could have taken.
The first pick becomes `dying` with the gain on it; a `victim` event carries its id; it may walk on until her star lands.
Each frame after: its death seen, dead; seen alive 1.2 s after the gain, let go and the gain moves on; unseen 0.3 s from 1.5 s on, dead.
A `died` event: kind, cause 'hers', x, platform, whether its death was seen.
In the command, after the look that drains the event, the chaser on that track is dropped; Memory marks it killed through the ledger's dead tracks.

flows.title: Newborns fading in teach the spawn clock
flows.summary: How a monster fading in at a spawn point becomes a timed pass in the SpawnClock, which the hunt's spawn guard and wait places ask.
flows.trigger: The server's spawn pass puts a monster on a free spawn point in view.

steps.text: The spawn watch looks at every spawn point in view (Tree Dungeon, 1366x768) and finds the newborn with its alpha, while the whole-screen search runs.
Newborns become detections (Mob.fading set) beside the whole screen's until the search finds them.
No track explains it: a new track, how 'spawned', and a `spawned` event carrying its `fading` alpha.
The event reaches the command with the look of its frame.
Through the hunter's `_births`: the birth is the event's time less alpha / 1.224; one found solid weighs 0.3.
Joins a pass within 0.4 s or starts a new one; fading births off a sure grid three passes running reset the clock.
When next asked: the densest phase, least squares on its inliers, the standard error.

The hunt's spawn guard (behavior.hunt `_respawn_guard`), once the clock is `sure`, takes the next pass and holds a trip to a pile whose stand would meet that pass's window by free spawn points, when going costs more than waiting.
Rule 9's wait places (`_respawn_wait`) are priced with the chance that the next second (`WAIT_AHEAD_S`, 1.0) meets a pass's window, through attack.danger.respawn_risk.

not_done: The service doesn't restart itself: a crash or its watchdog's exit stops perception until a client's `ensure` (10 s) or the babysitter starts another (README, The perception service: Not done).
A hang that holds Python's lock stops the watchdog thread too: clients drop after SILENT_S and stand still, and nothing ends that process. Not seen; the hangs tested offline let go of the lock.
The window's size is fixed at the service's first sight; the game restarted at another size waits for the user (or a service restart).

A monster the whole screen misses beside her (3.5% of the old re-finds' sightings, 6.4% within 50 units) is bridged by hidden tracks; the design's fallback (a masked match at a missed track's predicted box) was not built. The exact finder (worldstate.EXACT) now adds finds near her.
The simulator's monster walks and poses aren't calibrated to the user's clip yet (README, Perception at 15 frames a second: Not done).
The spawn watch, the exact finder and the halves run only at the game's own 1366x768; the spawn watch only on maps in perception.spawns.MEASURED (Tree Dungeon).

Aggro: the perception's bars kept from older reads put most wrong bars on unhurt monsters (97 of 118 at the arrivals); showing a bar only while fresh would change what fights see, and is to be measured.
Aggro and the spawn clock are not tried live: their numbers are the simulator's and replays of live hours.
The magician's aim is counted against her kill binding ('aim bound', 'aim elsewhere'), not measured with the service's own tracks yet.
SHARES (binding another player's kill of a monster she hurt) is off; POSE_GATE_S is an A/B switch left off.
Gains: a level-up during a hunt (the next level's requirement from the table) and an EXP event's rate check are to be checked in game.
Aggro's touches: a touch is damage unless its kind is 'miss' in lower case, while the touch watch says 'MISS', so a live MISS is taken for damage there (tests/test_aggro.py uses 'miss').
